topic: Template Function with Predicate for Range-Based Algorithms
explanation: This concept demonstrates how C++ uses function templates to create generic algorithms that operate over ranges defined by iterators. Specifically, the 'none_of' algorithm applies a predicate to each element in a range and returns true if none of the elements satisfy the predicate. Using templates allows this function to work with any iterator type and predicate, exemplifying C++'s emphasis on generic programming and type abstraction, especially in the context of the Standard Template Library (STL).
syntax:
template <class InputIterator, class Predicate>
bool none_of(InputIterator first, InputIterator last, Predicate pred);
example_explanation: This example defines a vector of integers and a lambda predicate 'is_even' to test for even numbers. It then uses 'std::none_of' with iterators to determine if none of the elements in the vector satisfy the predicate (i.e., are even). The program outputs 'Yes' because all numbers are odd, demonstrating how 'none_of' leverages templates and predicates to perform generic, range-based checks in modern C++.
